chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamadani quoted on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhdhal, on the authority of his father, who said: 'I asked Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him)'

about the reason why a woman who has been divorced three times cannot be married to her original husband again, until after she marries someone else. He said: 'Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, only granted permission for divorce twice.'
As the Honorable, the Exalted God says: 'A divorce is only permissible twice: after that, the parties should either hold together on equitable terms, or separate with kindness…'

Meaning in the third divorce, and for entering into what God dislikes for him, which is the third divorce, He made her unlawful for him. She will no longer be legitimate for him until after she marries someone else.
This is established so that the people do not underestimate divorce and do not misuse women.
ai.seo_question: What is the reason a woman divorced three times cannot return to her first husband until she marries someone else?
ai.summary: Imam Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) elucidates that the prohibition of *Tanzil* (returning to the first husband after the third divorce) serves as a divine safeguard against *Istikhfaf* (trivialization) of the divorce process. By requiring a new marriage and consummation, the ruling ensures that the third divorce is not merely a procedural formality for immediate reunion, thereby preventing couples from using it as a tool to test or manipulate each other without genuine commitment.
